chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani, who said:

I wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding marriage, so his letter came to me in his own handwriting: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: When there comes to you one whose manners and religion you are pleased with, marry him; if you do not, there will be strife in the land and great mischief.'
ai.seo_question: What are the criteria for accepting a marriage proposal in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in Al-Kafi, establishes a communal obligation for guardians to accept marriage proposals from those possessing good character and piety, highlighting the social imperative of preventing celibacy-induced disorder. The warning of 'fitnah' and 'fasad' underscores the Shia scholarly view that unchecked social instability arises from neglecting the institution of marriage, linking individual moral integrity directly to communal harmony.
